name: B01 blankQuotedStrings: a single quote opens nothing
why: a single-quoted string is no longer blanked: the enumerations, the stated rows and the silent-chunk rows with a single-quoted string

name: B02 blankQuotedStrings: a double quote opens nothing
why: a double-quoted string is no longer blanked

name: B03 blankQuotedStrings: the skip needs both a non-quote and a place before the memo (|| to &&)
why: any character at or after the memo is read as an opener of its own kind; on the long rows it reads every character as an opener and does not finish, so the runner reports KILLED (timeout): run it with a short --timeout or a --cmd that stops at the first failure

name: B04 blankQuotedStrings: the memo skips a start AT the stop too (< to <=)
why: not equivalent, which reading the code had called it: the memo STARTS at 0, so `<=` skips a start at the first character and a text that opens with a quote is never blanked (Learning 887: a label by reading is wrong in both directions)

name: B05 blankQuotedStrings: the memo skips the starts AFTER the stop (< to >)
why: a valid string after a failed read of the same kind is skipped, and the failed ones before it are read again; on the long rows it does not finish (KILLED by timeout): run it with a short --timeout or a --cmd that stops at the first failure

name: B06 blankQuotedStrings: the two kinds read each other's memo
why: a single-quoted string inside the stretch a double-quoted read failed over is skipped (`"'a'\` and U+2028); on the long rows it does not finish (KILLED by timeout): run it with a short --timeout or a --cmd that stops at the first failure

name: B07 blankQuotedStrings: the memo of the double quote is not kept
why: the output is the same but a run of 100,000 escaped double quotes before a failing end is read once for each: the clock rows of the oracle file (13 s against 3 s)

name: B08 blankQuotedStrings: the memo of the single quote is not kept
why: the same for 100,000 escaped single quotes

name: B09 blankQuotedStrings: the double memo stops one before the stop (-end - 1)
why: equivalent in answer and in cost: the only start the memo then lets through is the one just before the stop, whose read ends at the stop at once (its first character is the blocking backslash or the end of the text); argued from the code, not run

name: B11 blankQuotedStrings: a failed double read skips the next character too
why: a quote right after a double quote that opened nothing is never read: `"'x'`

name: B12 blankQuotedStrings: a failed single read skips the next character too
why: the same for a double quote right after a single quote that opened nothing

name: B13 blankQuotedStrings: the text before a string is dropped
why: everything between two strings is lost

name: B14 blankQuotedStrings: the copy resumes where the string began
why: the blanked string comes back after its blank

name: B15 blankQuotedStrings: the scan resumes on the closing quote
why: the closing quote opens a string of its own with the next quote

name: B16 blankQuotedStrings: the scan resumes one past the string
why: the first character after a string is never read: `"a""b"`

name: B17 blankQuotedStrings: a read that ended at 0 counts as a string (> to >=)
why: equivalent: a string ends at 2 or later and a failed read returns the negative of an index of at least 1, so the result is never 0; argued from the code, not run

name: B19 blankQuotedStrings: the tail after the last string is dropped
why: the text after the last string, and a text with no string at all, is lost

name: B20 blankQuotedStrings: the text comes back unchanged
why: no string is blanked

name: B21 blankQuotedStrings: the copy starts at 1
why: the first character is dropped from a text with no string

name: B22 blankQuotedStrings: the scan starts at 1
why: a string that opens at the first character is never read

name: B23 blankQuotedStrings: the loop reads one past the end (< to <=)
why: equivalent: past the end charCodeAt answers NaN, which is no quote, so the pass only steps; argued from the code, not run

name: B24 blankQuotedStrings: the loop stops before the last character (text.length - 1)
why: equivalent: a quote at the last index has nothing after it, so its read fails and sets a memo past the end that no later start could use; argued from the code, not run

name: B25 blankQuotedStrings: the double memo starts at 1
why: a double-quoted string at the first character is skipped

name: B26 blankQuotedStrings: the single memo starts at 1
why: a single-quoted string at the first character is skipped

name: B27 blankQuotedStrings: a string is blanked to two single quotes
why: the blank is no longer the empty double-quoted string the unnamed-argument test accepts

name: B28 blankQuotedStrings: a single start reads the double memo
why: a single-quoted string inside the stretch a double-quoted read failed over is skipped

name: Q01 quotedStringEnd: the body starts at the opener
from:
const quote = text.charCodeAt(open);
  let at = open + 1;
to:
const quote = text.charCodeAt(open);
  let at = open;
why: the opener closes its own string: every quote is blanked alone

name: Q02 quotedStringEnd: the body starts two past the opener
from:
const quote = text.charCodeAt(open);
  let at = open + 1;
to:
const quote = text.charCodeAt(open);
  let at = open + 2;
why: the first character of the body is never read: an empty string `""` does not close

name: Q03 quotedStringEnd: every string closes at a double quote
why: a single-quoted string holding a double quote closes early or never

name: Q04 quotedStringEnd: the end is the closing quote's own index
why: the closing quote stays in the text

name: Q05 quotedStringEnd: only a backslash steps by one
why: the body is read backwards: plain characters are taken as escapes

name: Q06 quotedStringEnd: an escape takes one character (at += 1)
why: the escaped quote closes the string: `"a\"b"`

name: Q07 quotedStringEnd: a line feed is no blocker
why: a backslash before a line feed is an escape: `"a\` + LF + `"` is blanked

name: Q08 quotedStringEnd: a carriage return is no blocker
why: a backslash before a carriage return is an escape

name: Q09 quotedStringEnd: U+2028 is no blocker
why: a backslash before U+2028 is an escape

name: Q10 quotedStringEnd: U+2029 is no blocker
why: a backslash before U+2029 is an escape

name: Q11 quotedStringEnd: a backslash as the last character is not a blocker (>= to >)
why: equivalent: the read then fails at the end of the text instead of at the backslash, one index later, and no quote sits between; argued from the code, not run

name: Q12 quotedStringEnd: a blocked read reports the end of the text
why: the memo then skips every later start of the kind, including the valid string after the blocker: `"a\` + U+2028 + `b" "c"`

name: Q13 quotedStringEnd: an unterminated read reports a place near the start
why: the memo no longer carries over the escaped quotes of an unterminated string: the clock rows of 100,000 pairs that never close

name: Q15 quotedStringEnd: the escaped character is the backslash itself
why: no line terminator ever blocks: a backslash before U+2028 is taken as an escape

name: C01 knitrHeaderOptions: the unnamed argument is not blanked
why: an unnamed string beside `echo=FALSE` is judged unread and the header is declined: the silent-chunk rows of qmd-model.test.ts and the Session 337 rows

name: C02 knitrHeaderOptions: the untrimmed segment is blanked
why: the blank keeps the space before the string, which the unnamed-argument test refuses

name: E02 oracle: seed 3371
why: the seeded counts are pinned for seed 3370

why: the pinned counts are those of five characters
